title: MySpace coming back — again — is no surprise; I’m only shocked it’s not been announced as the first all-AI social media platform
content_html:
Somewhere, Myspace Tom is looking over his shoulder, frowning. Everyone's first friend on the once-leading and iconic social and blogging platform, Tom Anderson's smiling face is the sole reminder of what Myspace once was. While so many loved its messy, GIF-filled countenance in 2004, it's unlikely he's cheering its potential comeback.

MySpace didn't survive the rise of Facebook (then "The Facebook"), let alone Tumblr, Twitter, and Instagram. Teens left in droves when NewsCorp bought it for $850M in 2005, and adults, who never understood it in the first place, stayed away by the millions. By 2011, it was sold for a measly $35M to a consortium that included Justin Timberlake. The shift to a more purely music-focused platform did little to distinguish or revive it. The domain survives, but according to Similarweb, it has just over 1.7M monthly uniques. That might sound like a lot, but it is a far cry from the 76M monthly visitors it enjoyed 20 years ago.

Now, Chris and Tim Vanderhook, who bought the platform with Timberlake in 2011, confirmed they plan to "relaunch Myspace."

Myspace version 3?

That, though, my friends, is not the surprising part. Companies relaunch valuable IP all the time in the quixotic belief that they can squeeze just a little more value or revenue out of it. It rarely goes their way.

No, what's truly astounding is that the Vanderhooks did not quickly follow that statement with, "It'll be built on an AI foundation."

I mean, seriously, what is the point of relaunching Myspace if not to house some new LLM, presumably one that connects in some fashion to music. Maybe a big partnership with — gag — Suno.

Myspace has, for the last 15 years, been all about music. The first menu item on the current site is "Featured," which is all about trending musicians, and the second menu item is "Music." "Videos", which is all clips of either "Getting Nailed" or "The Pedicab interviews," comes next, and "People," once the foundation of Myspace, comes last.

Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

If you happen to click on "People," Myspace encourages you to sign up with your Facebook account, which is the deepest cut of all when you consider how Facebook ate Myspace's lunch.

Profile types leave little room for the normies that once populated the platform: Your profile options include "Artists," "Writer". "DJ/producer," "Comedian," "Filmmaker," "Models," and similar extra types. It's like an Influencer reality show casting call. It's unclear how or if you can join as just a person.

If AI were a part of this promised next phase of MySpace, I assume it might help these influencer industry archetypes connect with their audiences and produce exactly the kind of content each wants and would consume at scale.

No way you'll recognize the next Myspace

I find it hard to imagine that the old-school Myspace, in all its chaotic luster, is somehow rising from the ashes. No online audience is still interested in that, right? Though, I guess a sort of anti-social media could work.

No algorithms, no filters, no cool interface, maybe even no AI, just point-to-point encrypted messages, space to say your piece, an occasional meme-worthy GIF, and that's all. It could be ever more bare-bones than the old Tumblr. I see no reason for that to exist, but at least it would stand out from the current selection of overwhelming communication and social media platforms.

Even so, in our current space, no technology is more energizing for investment and emergence than AI. So I fully expect the Vanderhooks, who are "just waiting for the right time to do it," to lean fully into the space and produce a Myspace-awkward blend of earnestness and AI.

They might even get Tom Anderson's permission to use his likeness in AI figures that show him looking over his shoulder, smiling and offering custom greetings on your Myspace page. Tom could be the platform's AI chatbot. It'll be creepy as heck and the polar opposite of what new Myspace should be, but I also see no other realistic path forward for this thing.

不过，我的朋友们，这并不是令人惊讶的部分。 公司一直在重新推出有价值的知识产权，他们不切实际地相信他们可以从中榨取更多的价值或收入。 事情很少能如他们所愿。

不，真正令人震惊的是，范德胡克夫妇并没有很快就说“它将建立在人工智能基础上”。

说真的，我的意思是，如果不是为了容纳一些新的法学硕士，可能是一个以某种方式与音乐相关的法学硕士，那么重新启动 Myspace 的意义何在。 也许与——搞笑——Suno有很大的合作关系。

过去 15 年里，Myspace 一直专注于音乐。 当前网站上的第一个菜单项是“精选”，全部与流行音乐家有关，第二个菜单项是“音乐”。 接下来是“视频”，即“Getting Nailed”或“The Pedicab Interviews”的所有剪辑，最后是“People”，曾经是 Myspace 的基础。

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

如果您碰巧点击“人员”，Myspace 会鼓励您使用 Facebook 帐户进行注册，当您考虑到 Facebook 是如何吃掉 Myspace 的午餐时，这是最深刻的切入点。

个人资料类型为曾经在平台上占据一席之地的普通人留下了很少的空间：您的个人资料选项包括“艺术家”、“作家”。 “DJ/制作人”、“喜剧演员”、“电影制片人”、“模特”以及类似的额外类型。 这就像有影响力的真人秀选角。 目前尚不清楚您如何或是否可以作为个人加入。

如果人工智能是 MySpace 承诺的下一阶段的一部分，我认为它可能会帮助这些有影响力的行业原型与他们的受众建立联系，并准确地生产出每个人想要并愿意大规模消费的内容。

您不可能认出下一个 Myspace

我很难想象老派的 Myspace，在其混乱的光彩下，会以某种方式从灰烬中重生。 没有在线观众仍然对此感兴趣，对吧？ 不过，我想某种反社交媒体可能会起作用。

没有算法，没有过滤器，没有炫酷的界面，甚至可能没有人工智能，只有点对点的加密消息，表达你的观点的空间，偶尔一个值得模仿的 GIF，仅此而已。 它可能比旧的 Tumblr 更加简陋。 我认为没有理由存在这种情况，但至少它会从当前铺天盖地的通信和社交媒体平台中脱颖而出。

即便如此，在我们当前的领域，没有任何技术比人工智能更能促进投资和崛起。 因此，我完全期待范德胡克夫妇“只是在等待合适的时机去做这件事”，能够完全投入到这个领域，并创造出一个将真诚与人工智能结合在一起的 Myspace 尴尬的组合。

他们甚至可能会得到汤姆·安德森的许可，在人工智能人物中使用他的肖像，让他在你的 Myspace 页面上回头看、微笑并提供定制问候。 汤姆可能是该平台的人工智能聊天机器人。 这会令人毛骨悚然，与新的 Myspace 应该有的样子截然相反，但我也认为这件事没有其他现实的前进道路。
